executiveSummary.text: US risk regime remains constructive after S&P 500 closed at 7,757.64 (+0.62%) and Nasdaq 26,690.62 (+1.30%) on Friday; VIX eased to 14.9. CNBC notes the S&P finished Friday at an all-time closing high and this week’s focus shifts to July CPI. Base case: risk-on but CPI-fragile, not a blanket chase signal.

Rates/liquidity are the swing factor: 10Y Treasury ~4.66% Friday close via Yahoo vs FRED latest 4.69% on Aug 6; 30Y ~5.21%; 10Y real yield latest 2.43%; DXY ~99.63. Softer labor headlines support cut hopes, but sticky inflation/term-premium risk can still cap multiples.

AI/semis are still leadership, but the fresh news flow is about capex validation and rotation discipline rather than a new shock: Yahoo/Investing coverage highlights AI infrastructure and CPI as the week’s two key tests, while MU/auto-AI demand commentary remains supportive. KL should keep scarcity exposure but avoid adding into euphoric gaps.

Singapore remains a portfolio tailwind: STI +1.05% Friday; OCBC +3.31% crossed KL’s abnormal-move threshold after strong H1/Q2 bank results, while DBS +1.66% and UOB -0.64%. SG bank thesis intact, but valuation/yield compression argues for HOLD not chase.
Scarcity assets are bid: GLD +2.26%, SLV +2.95%, COPX +2.25%, URNM +2.77% crossed ETF thresholds. This is a real-rate/USD/liquidity and scarcity-chain move, not just a “safe haven” story.

Geopolitics is market-relevant through energy/shipping: fresh Reuters/Investing reports oil rising on uncertainty over Strait reopening; crude is up modestly (WTI +0.69%, Brent +0.86%), so the inflation transmission is present but not yet regime-breaking.

regime.label: Risk-on, CPI-sensitive melt-up with rates as the volatility trigger

usGlobal.what: US equities ended last week with a broad risk-on tone; S&P at a record close per CNBC, Nasdaq led, Russell +1.10%.
usGlobal.why: Weak jobs narrative lowered hike fears and pulled forward rate-cut optionality; mega-cap/AI leadership remains intact.
usGlobal.implication: Stay invested; add only on CPI/rate-driven pullbacks rather than chasing a low-VIX record-close tape.

ratesMacro.what: This week’s July CPI is the main macro event. FRED shows latest 10Y real yield still high at 2.43%, with breakevens 2.25%.
ratesMacro.why: Equities can tolerate high real yields only while earnings/AI capex remain strong; a CPI upside surprise would raise discount rates and pressure long-duration AI/REIT assets.
ratesMacro.implication: Do not overread Friday’s risk-on move until CPI confirms disinflation or at least no re-acceleration.

asiaSingapore.what: Singapore bank strength remains the dominant STI driver; Business Times/Straits Times fresh coverage highlights DBS and OCBC strength after H1/Q2 results and a wealth-management boom.
asiaSingapore.why: Higher-for-longer net interest margins plus wealth fees support earnings, but dividend yields compress when prices run.
asiaSingapore.implication: SG dividend sleeve is doing its ballast job; rotate incremental dollars only if laggards/REITs offer better forward yield after rates ease.

commodities.what: Gold/silver/copper miners/uranium ETFs rose materially; oil is only modestly higher despite Hormuz uncertainty.
commodities.why: Precious metals respond to real-rate and USD path; copper/uranium remain tied to AI power/grid scarcity; oil needs sustained physical disruption to become a broader inflation shock.
commodities.implication: Keep scarcity basket; use spikes to rebalance only if position sizing breaches comfort bands.

geopolitics.what: Fresh Reuters/Investing and regional headlines cite uncertainty over Strait reopening and Red Sea/Houthi risk.
geopolitics.why: Transmission path is freight insurance, tanker routing, jet fuel, and inflation expectations—not a mechanical gold bid.
geopolitics.implication: If Brent moves above prior stress levels with widening breakevens, trim rate-sensitive tactical exposure and avoid levered REIT risk.

moves.what: OCBC +3.31% on Aug 7, above individual holding threshold.
moves.why: Fresh Singapore bank coverage points to strong H1/Q2 results, wealth-management fees, and dividend/yield support.
moves.implication: Strengthens SG dividend sleeve; 2nd order: STI concentration rises and forward dividend yields compress; 3rd order: rotation may emerge into non-bank STI/REIT laggards if rates fall.
moves.action: HOLD; add only on earnings-quality confirmation plus valuation reset; trim only if bank sleeve becomes oversized or credit cycle turns.

moves.what: GLD +2.26% and SLV +2.95% on Aug 7; silver ETF near the abnormal ETF threshold by a wide margin.
moves.why: Rate-cut hopes, softer USD/real-rate expectations, and scarcity/monetary-hedge demand. Not a simple crisis trade.
moves.implication: Supports KL’s scarcity sleeve and portfolio ballast against policy error; 2nd order: if real yields fall, long-duration equities also benefit; if inflation breakevens rise instead, equities may not.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on pullback with falling real yields or policy credibility concerns; TRIM if real yields break higher and USD rallies together.

moves.why: Scarcity basket beta improved as AI power/grid and electrification narratives stayed firm; uranium remains tied to nuclear/power-security demand.
moves.implication: Positive for KL’s “own what AI depends on” thesis; 2nd order: power constraints raise capex for hyperscalers; 3rd order: grid/power bottlenecks can shift AI winners toward firms with secured energy.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on commodity-specific drawdowns, not after broad risk-on days; invalidator is demand destruction plus project supply acceleration.

thesisImpact.what: AI scarcity thesis remains intact but valuation-sensitive.
thesisImpact.why: Semicap/equipment names rose but mostly below abnormal thresholds; leadership is healthy but crowded.
thesisImpact.implication: Maintain diversified semis/hyperscaler/EDA exposure; NVDA underweight remains acceptable because thesis is supply-chain breadth, not one-stock heroics.
thesisImpact.action: HOLD / selective ADD on CPI-led multiple compression.

narratives.title: CPI is now more important than last week’s jobs relief
narratives.description: Markets rallied as weak labor data lowered hike fears, but July CPI will decide whether lower yields are justified or whether inflation risk re-prices term premium. Scenario weights: 55% benign CPI/risk-on continuation; 30% sticky CPI/range-bound chop; 15% upside CPI/rate shock. Confidence: medium.

narratives.title: AI capex durability versus valuation digestion
narratives.description: AI infrastructure remains the earnings pillar, but multiples need low/stable real yields. 2nd order: if hyperscaler capex persists, semicap/equipment/memory benefit; 3rd order: power/grid scarcity shifts economics toward energy-secured data-center operators and suppliers.

narratives.title: Singapore banks are quality winners but less cheap
narratives.description: Fresh local coverage highlights strong results and wealth-fee tailwinds. The underpriced question is not whether banks are good, but whether incremental expected return is now lower after a concentrated rally.
narratives.source: Business Times, Straits Times, Singapore Business Review

narratives.title: Hormuz risk is inflation transmission, not a slogan
narratives.description: Oil is only modestly higher so far. Market damage requires sustained physical disruption: oil/freight up -> breakevens up -> yields/term premium up -> REITs and long-duration tech multiple pressure.

secondOrderEffects.text: If CPI is soft, lower nominal/real yields can lift both QQQ/semis and GLD/SLV together; that is a liquidity/discount-rate move, not contradictory risk-on plus safe-haven behavior.
secondOrderEffects.implication: KL can let both growth and scarcity sleeves work; avoid forcing an either/or narrative.

secondOrderEffects.text: If oil shock widens breakevens while real yields stay high, equities face a worse mix: inflation tax plus no discount-rate relief.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Watch Brent, 10Y breakevens, and USD together before adding REITs or long-duration tech.

secondOrderEffects.text: Singapore bank outperformance increases STI concentration; if global rates fall, the second-order rotation may be toward REITs and lagging industrials rather than more banks.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Fresh cash should require better entry points in DBS/OCBC/UOB; keep REIT watchlist alive.

investment.thesis: Maintain broad global equity core plus scarcity/AI supply-chain barbell.
investment.trigger: Add VWRA/QQQ/semicap basket on 5–10% drawdowns caused by rate/CPI fear without thesis impairment.
investment.whyNow: Risk regime is favorable but record-close/low-VIX entries have weaker margin of safety.
investment.invalidator: AI capex cuts broaden across hyperscalers or real yields rise persistently above earnings yield support.

investment.thesis: Keep SG banks as income ballast but redirect incremental Singapore adds toward REITs only when rates confirm easing.
investment.trigger: 10Y yields decline with no credit stress and Singapore REIT NAV discounts remain wide.
investment.whyNow: Bank valuations/yields have compressed after strong rally; REITs are cleaner rate-duration plays if easing arrives.
investment.invalidator: Funding spreads widen, occupancy weakens, or inflation re-accelerates.

trading.thesis: CPI week favors patience over chasing.
trading.trigger: If CPI is benign and 10Y breaks lower, add a small tactical QQQ/semicap tranche; if CPI hot and 10Y/DXY spike, wait for forced selling.
trading.whyNow: Market is already priced for good news after record close.
trading.invalidator: No move in rates/USD after CPI.

trading.thesis: Oil geopolitical risk hedge only if physical disruption becomes visible in prices.
trading.trigger: Brent closes materially higher with freight/insurance stress and breakevens rising.
trading.whyNow: Headlines are severe but crude move is still modest.
trading.invalidator: Strait reopening or oil fades despite headlines.

watchlist.thesis: Real-yield pivot determines whether metals rally has legs.
watchlist.trigger: 10Y real yield falls below recent range while DXY weakens.
watchlist.invalidator: Real yields and USD rise together.

watchlist.trigger: Hyperscaler commentary mentions grid/power as binding constraint or capex shifts to energy-secured sites.
watchlist.invalidator: Power supply catches up faster than data-center demand.

riskWatch.name: CPI/term-premium shock
riskWatch.description: Sticky inflation with high real yields would pressure long-duration AI, REITs, and risk multiples.
riskWatch.mitigation: Keep cash dry powder; add in tranches only after rate confirmation.

riskWatch.name: AI capex crowding
riskWatch.description: AI winners remain fundamentally strong, but crowded positioning can cause sharp valuation resets even without thesis damage.
riskWatch.mitigation: Prefer diversified semis/EDA/equipment/hyperscaler exposure; avoid single-name FOMO.

riskWatch.name: Hormuz/energy inflation transmission
riskWatch.description: A sustained oil/shipping disruption can lift breakevens and complicate Fed easing.
riskWatch.mitigation: Monitor Brent, freight rates, breakevens, USD; do not assume gold automatically hedges every shock.

keyEvents.text: July CPI due this week; CNBC/Investing.com flag it as the market’s next key test after weak jobs relief.
Singapore bank results/wealth fees continue to drive DBS and OCBC strength; OCBC +3.31% crossed KL abnormal-move threshold.
Oil up modestly as Reuters/Investing reports uncertainty over Strait reopening; inflation impact not yet regime-breaking.

bottomLine.whatMatters: CPI, real yields, DXY, AI capex durability, and whether Hormuz risk becomes a real oil/freight inflation shock.
bottomLine.whatToDo: Stay invested; keep cash ballast; HOLD OCBC/SG banks and scarcity ETFs; add only on rate/CPI-driven pullbacks with intact thesis.
bottomLine.whatToIgnore: One-day record-close excitement, generic “geopolitics = gold up” heuristics, and pressure to fix deliberate NVDA underweight.
